analysis.body:
Per the Census Bureau's BTOS series, 16.0% of construction firms in NAICS 23 reported using AI in the latest survey period, up from 14.3% in the prior period. The survey asks whether a business used AI in the last two weeks, and the series first asked the question in September 2023, so the trend is measured directly from firms rather than estimated.

The sources point to a narrow set of deployment areas. BuiltWorlds tracks site robotics, jobsite IoT, and digital preconstruction across its research programs and member benchmarking. AGC surveys technology adoption and safety-technology compliance across US builders. This site's coverage, drawing on AGC, BuiltWorlds, and the proptech and contech trackers, highlights computer-vision safety monitoring, BIM clash detection, and autonomous site scanning as the areas where construction AI activity is concentrated.

Vendor and investor attention clusters around industry events and networks. CREtech and MetaProp track venture flow across architecture, engineering, and construction technology alongside property tech. CREtech New York 2026 describes itself as the premier real estate AI conference, expecting 3,000 leaders, 150 speakers, and 20,000+ pre-scheduled 1:1 meetings, with sponsors and partners representing companies shaping real estate in the age of AI. BuiltWorlds runs an annual AI/ML Conference and a Buildings Conference that emphasizes data centers and AI infrastructure, including case studies and implementation strategies.

The excerpts do not report quantified ROI figures. BuiltWorlds points to case studies illustrating how companies use specific solutions and the lessons learned, and a 2026 session titled "Quick Wins, Lasting Change: Founders Showcasing AI's Practical Power in Construction" suggests practical applications, but no return numbers are published in these sources. A reader deciding whether to deploy should treat the Census figure as the measured baseline, 16.0% of construction firms reporting recent AI use, and rely on member benchmarking and case studies rather than public ROI benchmarks.

The sources are silent on AI-specific risk and regulatory posture. AGC's recent survey reports construction input costs climbed 8.9% between August 2025 and August 2026 and construction unemployment hit a record low of 3.1%, with firms struggling to fill openings, but these are broader operating conditions and are not connected to AI risk in the excerpts.

https://cretech.com/.brief: According to the page, CREtech New York 2026 will be held at the Javits Center in New York City on October 20, 21, 2026, and will bring together 3,000 leaders, 150 speakers, and more than 20,000 pre-scheduled 1:1 meetings. The event is described as a leading real-estate AI conference where sessions are led by operators actively deploying AI in their portfolios, offering real strategy rather than theory. The conference aims to connect owners, developers, investors, occupiers, construction firms, brokers, and tech leaders to discuss AI’s impact on real-estate assets. Tickets are limited, and sponsors and partners are said to represent companies shaping the future of real-estate in the age of AI.

https://www.agc.org/.brief: The Associated General Contractors of America describes a leadership course for project executives and a connected platform for heavy civil and infrastructure work. The group says it has over 27,000 member firms and provides services to address member needs and protect the public interest. According to an association survey, construction input costs rose 8.9% between August 2025 and August 2026, with war and tariff impacts disrupting projects. The association also reports contractors added 22,000 jobs in August and the construction unemployment rate hit a record low of 3.1%, while firms struggle to fill openings.

https://builtworlds.com/.brief: BuiltWorlds operates a membership network for buildings and infrastructure professionals. The organization hosts an annual Buildings Conference addressing innovation in building development, design, materials and systems, with particular focus on data centers and AI infrastructure. It also runs an annual AI/ML Conference exploring artificial intelligence and machine learning adoption across the architecture, engineering, construction and operations industry, covering implementation strategies, use cases, and lessons learned from companies deploying these technologies.
